headline: The trail block ran longer than the last read suggested — multiple back-to-back ultra-distance days at controlled HR are now logged. The engine held its shape throughout. Absorption is the next real question.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is dominated by a large, sustained block of time on foot at deliberately controlled intensity — long days stacked back-to-back, all sitting almost entirely in the lowest zone despite the distances. That's durability work executing exactly as intended, not racing. Steps are correspondingly high and barely differ between run and rest days, confirming these are genuinely active days rather than true rest. Strength, though, has gone quiet — the log shows nothing recent, and its absence is now the clearest open thread against a background where the running side is doing heavy lifting. The Polar strain reading collapsing to a detraining flag is an artefact of how it windows load, not a real signal here given what's actually in the run log; treat it as noise this week. Sleep across the block was broken and short on several nights, which is unsurprising given the demands and worth watching now that the big days appear to be tapering.
sections.trends: Year-to-date volume is running far ahead of the same point last year, and the recent four-week block is up sharply on the prior one — a large, deliberate build driven by this trail effort rather than a steady ramp. That shape is cyclical and event-shaped rather than linear, which fits an athlete who builds durability in concentrated blocks and then absorbs. The key is that this spike lands on top of a genuinely deep base, so the jump reads as a peak within a long consistent trend, not an overreach from a standing start.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the VO2-adjacent markers are unchanged from baseline, which is expected — nothing in the recent block was designed to move them. Weeks of very low-intensity, high-volume work don't sharpen threshold and shouldn't be read as having dulled it either. The demonstrated speed is still sitting where it was; it simply hasn't been touched. When faster work re-enters, that's where you'll see whether the aerobic base built here translates upward.
sections.zones: The distribution is almost entirely Zone 1, with only trace amounts higher — and for what this block was trying to do, that's correct. The per-session shapes confirm it: even the longest and highest-climbing days stayed low, with only the very first big day and one shorter effort nudging briefly into Z2. This is textbook durability-block intensity control — the risk in this kind of work is drifting upward as fatigue accumulates, and that didn't happen. There's essentially no grey-zone contamination here.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR from the most recent sessions sits where these functional sessions usually land — moderate average, brief excursions upward — consistent with prior sessions of the same type. Across the run block the HR shapes are internally coherent and match the paces and terrain, with no odd divergences between sources worth flagging. Nothing anomalous in the HR data this week.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows a dense, uninterrupted run of consecutive training days through the block — the interleaved run/strength rhythm has been temporarily replaced by continuous time on foot. That's appropriate for a concentrated durability effort, but it also explains why strength dropped out: the block crowded it. The thing to watch now is whether the normal alternating pattern re-establishes rather than the running simply continuing at volume without strength folding back in.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current bests are within reach off the back of this block — the recent work is the opposite end of the spectrum from the short, fast efforts that set the 5K and 10K marks. Those PBs remain a function of speed work that hasn't been the focus lately. The ultra-distance bests, by contrast, are directly served by exactly this kind of accumulated durability, so this block quietly strengthens that side of the profile even without a new mark logged.

watch_items: Watch whether strength genuinely re-enters the log now that the concentrated foot volume is easing, rather than staying crowded out.
Watch whether easy-run HR settles back to normal for its pace as the big days taper, confirming the block is being absorbed cleanly.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the block's short, broken nights should be behind you.
Watch whether the calendar returns to its interleaved rhythm rather than extending continuous running volume.
